column1: # Numbered supplementary tables, in manuscript order.
# This file defines table numbers and display names. `make final-outputs` and `make supplementary`
# run tools/package_supplementary_tables.py, which copies each `source` out of figure_data/ as
# and writes a one-line folder README pointing to Supplementary Information.pdf. Renumbering means editing a column here,
# not renaming a file: the figure_data/ filename is the stage-1 contract read by producers,
# PROVENANCE.md and verify-tables. final_plots/ is hashed and is not part of this packaging path.
# Columns are TAB-separated. `description` is required but not written to the package; the
# table descriptions live in Supplementary Information.pdf.
# `source` is one filename, or a multi-sheet spec `Sheet name=file.csv;Other=other.csv` packaged
# as one .xlsx. The sheet CSVs live separately in figure_data/ and combine at package time: an
# xlsx is not byte-reproducible, since each zip member stores a wall-clock timestamp. Keeping the
# workbook out of figure_data/ and final_plots/ keeps `make verify-tables` from reporting a
# reproduction failure on every run. The workbook itself is not hashed.

column4: Provided as external file. Genes and their IGNITE positive-unlabeled prioritization scores are described in the table, one row per gene. Variable "pu_score" is the mean predicted probability across bagging iterations, taken out-of-bag where the gene was not drawn as a pseudo-negative that iteration; the 340 approved genes are in-bag every iteration, so their scores are optimistic and are recorded only so the ranking has a value for them. Variables "rank" and "rank_pctile" give the corresponding genome-wide rank (1 = highest score) and rank percentile. Variable "drug_status" records the immune-indication label (approved, in-trial, non-target), variable "pu_role" the role of the gene in model fitting (training positive, held-out in-trial, unlabeled), and variable "furthest_imm_stage" the most advanced immune-indication trial phase reached by any drug annotated to the gene. Genetic-block variables are "IEI" (binary membership of the IUIS inborn-errors-of-immunity gene list), "gwas_score" (immune system disorder association score, MONDO:0005046), "gene_burden_score" (rare-variant burden association score for immune indications, from the Open Targets gene_burden datasource), "mis.z_score" (missense Z-score) and "lof.oe_ci.upper" (LOEUF). Observational variables "zscore_Th1", "zscore_Th2", "zscore_Th17" and "zscore_Treg" are differential-expression z-scores of each polarized T-helper subset against resting Th0 (Th = T helper, Treg = regulatory T cell). Perturbational variables "polar_coef_rank_Rest", "polar_coef_rank_Stim8hr" and "polar_coef_rank_Stim48hr" are ranked polarization coefficients at rest and after 8 h and 48 h of stimulation, with their range in "polar_rank_range"; variables "reg_burden_sig_*" indicate a significant lymphocyte-count loss-of-function burden correlation per condition; variables "n_sig_regulated_cytokines_*" and "n_sig_regulated_cytokine_receptors_*" count significantly regulated cytokines and cytokine receptors per condition; variable "expected_n_regulators_residuals" is the residual between observed and expected number of trans-regulators, averaged across conditions; and variable "has_cytokine" is the coverage indicator for genes with cytokine and cytokine-receptor data. Variables "crossdonor_confidence" and "crossdonor_correlation_mean" carry the cross-donor reproducibility annotation of the perturbation signature and are identical by construction, blank for 16,973 of the 19,502 genes. All functional-genomic values were derived from the genome-scale CD4+ T-cell perturb-seq resource of Zhu, Dann et al., 2025; constraint values were derived from the gnomAD v4.1.0 gene constraint metrics table.

Provided as external file. The 24 modelled features are described in the table, one row per feature. Variable "feature" is the column name as it appears in the feature matrix and in Supplementary Table 1, and variable "block" assigns the feature to one of three evidence blocks (genetic, 5 features; observational functional genomics, 4 features; perturbational functional genomics, 15 features). Variable "condition" indicates the stimulation context of the measurement (Rest, Stim8hr, Stim48hr, or an across-condition summary) and is empty for features without a condition. Variable "type" records whether the feature is binary or continuous, variable "definition" gives the quantity measured and any transformation applied, and variable "observed_rho" the observed Spearman correlation between the feature and "pu_score" over genes with an observed value. That correlation is empirical rather than a prespecified expected sign: gradient-boosted gain importance is unsigned, so the model supplies no direction of its own. Variables "n_nonmissing" and "pct_nonmissing" account for the number and percentage of the 19,502 genes with an observed value; note that "IEI" and "has_cytokine" are stored as integers and cannot carry missing values, so their complete coverage is a storage property rather than evidence of complete measurement, and that "gwas_score" is fully observed but 54-64% zero-inflated by drug-status group. Variable "imputation" states the rule applied to missing entries (training-row median within each bagging iteration; zero for columns entirely missing within a fit). Variable "source" names the originating resource and release. Block membership as given here is the definition asserted at every attribution-decomposition step, so that all non-metadata columns are covered exactly once. Per-feature importance means and standard deviations across bagging iterations are reported in the accompanying variables "imp_mean" and "imp_sd"; these are normalized gain, so "imp_mean" sums to 1.0 across the 24 features, and "imp_sd" is a population standard deviation across bagging iterations rather than a standard error.

column3: Drug-status labels and immune-indication trial annotations
column4: Provided as external file. Genes and their immune-indication development status are described in the table, one row per gene with any immune-indication drug annotation (1,089 genes). Variable "drug_status" is the assigned label (approved, in-trial, non-target) and variable "furthest_imm_stage" the most advanced immune-indication trial phase reached by any drug annotated to the gene, with genes whose per-gene furthest-stage annotation was unknown treated as non-target. Variable "n_drugs" accounts for the total number of immune-indication drugs annotated to the gene and variable "drug_names" lists them; variable "indications" lists the corresponding disease terms. Variable "first_trial_year" gives the earliest trial start year across those drugs in any condition, not only the immune indication, and variable "approval_year" the year of first approval where applicable, populated for 332 of the 340 approved genes. Variable "multi_target_expanded" flags genes entered through expansion of a multi-target drug, defined as genes reached by no single-target drug annotation, and variable "in_feature_matrix" indicates presence in the 19,502-gene matrix; the seven mitochondrially encoded in-trial genes absent from the nuclear feature matrix are retained with this variable set to false. Labels and trial annotations were derived from the Open Targets Platform 26.06 evidence tables.

column3: Univariate feature statistics by drug status
column4: Provided as external file, one sheet per panel of Figures 2 and 3, together with one test sheet each for Figures 2b, 2c, 3a and 3b and two summary sheets for Figures 3c and 3d. Genes, their drug-status group and the corresponding feature values are described in the gene-level sheets: variable "group" is the drug-status group (approved, in-trial, non-target), and variables "gwas_score", "mis_z_score" and "residual" carry the immune-GWAS score, the missense Z-score and the trans-regulatory burden residual respectively. The immune-GWAS sheet covers all 19,502 genes, an absent score being recorded as zero; Figure 2b itself plots only the 7,170 genes scoring above zero, so that sheet describes the full distribution rather than the panel as drawn. In the T-helper sheet, variable "subset" is the polarized subset compared against resting Th0 and variable "neglog10_adjp" the negative base-10 logarithm of the adjusted differential-expression p-value. The Figure 3a test sheet dichotomizes that same "neglog10_adjp" at 10% FDR and asks, within each subset, whether a target class reaches the threshold more often than non-target genes: variable "subset" is the polarized subset, variable "group" the drug-status group with two additional summary levels ("all tested genes" for the subset's marginal rate and "non-target" for the Fisher reference), variables "n_tested" and "n_hit" the genes tested in that subset and the subset of those reaching 10% FDR, variable "pct_hit" the latter as a percentage of the former, variable "OR" the two-sided Fisher sample odds ratio against non-target genes with variables "OR_lo" and "OR_hi" bounding its Woolf 95% CI, and variable "p" for the raw Fisher p-value and variable "p_holm" for the same p after Holm-Bonferroni correction. Each target class is one pre-specified family of four subsets and is corrected independently, so "p_holm" on an approved row is never a function of an in-trial p-value; the significance claims in the Figure 3a text are applied to "p_holm". The panel itself draws no significance annotation, so this sheet carries no star column. Because "n_tested" counts genes measured in that subset alone, it is smaller than the group size on the Figure 3a facet strip and varies between subsets; the marginal and reference rows have no odds ratio against themselves and so carry empty CI and p cells. The two Figure 2 test sheets compare those same feature values between drug-status groups in long format, one row per test with the omnibus first, sharing the column vocabulary of the Figure 3b test sheet described below. Variable "genes" records which genes each row was computed on, because the Figure 2b sheet has two blocks. Its first block asks who carries any immune-GWAS signal at all: three two-sided Fisher tests on all genes, where variables "n_gt0_a", "n_gt0_b", "pct_gt0_a" and "pct_gt0_b" are the counts and percentages above zero and variables "OR", "OR_lo" and "OR_hi" the odds ratio with its Woolf 95% interval. Its second block asks how large the signal is when present, and is restricted to genes with a score above zero because that is the subset the Figure 2b panel draws; it reports the same rank statistics as the Figure 3b sheet. The two blocks are corrected separately, three tests each, because they test different quantities: reading only one misleads, since approved and in-trial targets are indistinguishable in whether they carry signal yet differ in how much. Because "gwas_score" is fully observed and never imputed, a zero is a measured absence of association rather than a missing value, which is what makes the first block a test rather than a filtering step. The Figure 2c sheet needs no such split, as no gene carries a missense Z-score of exactly zero. Note that "mis_z_score" is not fully observed the way "gwas_score" is: 75 genes, all non-target, have no missense Z-score and are absent from that panel, so its non-target group is 18,360 genes against the 18,435 of the Figure 2b Fisher block. The Figure 3b test sheet compares that same "residual" between drug-status groups in long format, one row per test with the omnibus first: variable "test" names the test, variables "group_a" and "group_b" the two groups compared with the reference group second, variables "n_a" and "n_b" their sizes and variables "median_a" and "median_b" their medians, variable "hl_shift" the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift between them with variables "hl_lo" and "hl_hi" bounding its Wilcoxon rank-sum 95% interval, variable "p_sup" the probability that a randomly drawn gene from group_a exceeds one from group_b with variables "p_sup_lo" and "p_sup_hi" bounding its Hanley-McNeil 95% interval, variables "statistic" and "value" the test statistic and its value, and variables "p", "p_holm" and "stars" the raw p-value, the same p after Holm-Bonferroni correction across the three pairwise comparisons as one family, and the corresponding star rung. The Kruskal-Wallis row is the omnibus across all three groups, is left uncorrected, and carries empty cells in every pairwise column; the rank-biserial correlation is not reported because it equals twice "p_sup" minus one and would restate that column. The two Figure 3c/3d summary sheets describe those count distributions, which are too zero-inflated for the location tests used on Figures 3a and 3b: at 88-94% zeros every median and location-shift estimate is exactly zero, so what separates the groups is how often a gene regulates anything and how heavy the tail is when it does. On both sheets variable "panel" names the panel and variable "condition" the stimulation context. On the distribution sheet, variables "n" and "n_reg" are the genes measured in that condition and the subset regulating at least one target, variable "pct_reg" their percentage and variable "pct_zero" its complement, variable "mean" the group mean plotted as the panel's diamond, variable "mean_nonzero" that mean restricted to regulating genes, and variables "max" and "n_ge3" the largest count and the number of genes regulating three or more targets; these last two are what show that a group mean can rest on a handful of genes. On the regulator-fraction sheet, variable "group" is the target class tested and variables "n_ref", "n_reg_ref" and "pct_reg_ref" describe the non-target genes it is tested against in the same condition, variables "OR", "OR_lo" and "OR_hi" the odds ratio of regulating anything with its Woolf 95% interval, and variables "p", "p_holm" and "stars" the two-sided Fisher p-value, the same p after Holm-Bonferroni correction across the two target classes within that condition as one family, and the corresponding star rung. The counts on these sheets are per condition and so are smaller than the distinct-gene totals on the Figure 3c and 3d facet strips. Note that these two sheets count regulation outgoing from a gene, the cytokines or receptors it regulates, whereas the Figure 3b sheets count regulators incoming to a gene; the word points in opposite directions within one figure. In the cytokine sheets, variable "condition" is the stimulation context and variable "n_sig" the count of significantly regulated cytokines or cytokine receptors. The enrichment sheet reports variable "background" (all other genes, or the druggable genome as defined by Finan et al., 2017), variables "n" and "n_iei" for group size and number of IEI genes, variable "OR" for the two-sided Fisher sample odds ratio with variables "OR_lo" and "OR_hi" bounding its Woolf 95% CI, and variable "p" for the raw Fisher p-value and variable "p_holm" for the same p after Holm-Bonferroni correction across the four (group x background) enrichment cells, which are one pre-specified family; the star ladder drawn on Figure 2a is applied to "p_holm". Its two background reference rows have no odds ratio against themselves and so carry empty CI and p cells. Variable "pct_gt0" accounts for the percentage of genes in each group with a non-zero immune-GWAS score, and is the complement of the zero-inflation rate quoted in the Methods. Group sizes for every panel are given in the accompanying sheet by variables "panel", "group" and "n"; the reported n is the number of genes with data for a given assay and therefore varies between panels, and is a row count rather than a distinct-gene count for the regulatory-residual panel.

column3: Orthogonality of functional-genomic evidence to genetic priors
column4: Provided as external file. Every pairing of a genetic prior with a functional-genomic feature is described in the first sheet, one row per pair. Variable "genetic" names the genetic prior and variable "fg" the functional-genomic feature; variable "n" accounts for the number of genes with both values observed, and differs between pairs because feature coverage differs. Variable "rho" is the Spearman correlation coefficient with its p-value in variable "p", and variable "shared_var_pct" the percentage of shared variance implied by that coefficient. A second sheet describes the pairings among the five genetic priors themselves: variables "feature_1" and "feature_2" name the pair, variables "axis_1" and "axis_2" assign each to an evidence axis (rare-variant (curated), rare-variant (burden), common-variant, or evolutionary constraint), variable "relation" records whether the pair spans two axes or sits within one, and variables "spearman_rho", "spearman_p", "pearson_r" and "shared_variance_pct_spearman" report the correlation statistics. The single within-axis pair is gnomAD LOEUF against gnomAD missense Z, which share roughly half their rank variance because both measure depletion of variation; that is why they constitute one axis rather than two. The two rare-variant priors are by contrast held as separate axes, curated IEI membership and the gene-burden association, because they share only 0.34% of their rank variance, no more than a pair spanning two axes; grouping them would assert a relationship the data does not carry.

column3: Cross-validated performance of all evidence coalitions and attribution
column4: Provided as external file. All eight coalitions of the three evidence blocks are described in the first sheet, one row per coalition, with the empty coalition fixed at chance performance and carrying a standard deviation of zero by definition rather than by estimation. Variable "coalition" names the blocks included, and variables "auc_mean" and "auc_sd" give the mean cross-validated AUC and its population standard deviation across the 25 samples (five folds x five seeds). In the model-ladder sheet, variable "model" identifies the model variant, variable "label" its display label, and variables "auc", "sd" and "sem" the mean AUC, standard deviation and standard error. The significance sheet reports variables "model_a" and "model_b" for the compared variants, variable "delta" for the paired change in AUC, variable "nb_p" for the Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled paired t-test p-value, and variable "stars" for the corresponding significance annotation. Attribution variables are "evidence" (evidence block), "shapley_auc" (exact block-level grouped-Shapley value of AUC-above-chance) and "share_pct" (its percentage share); the three Shapley values sum exactly to the full model's AUC above chance. A final sheet describes the per-block stratum analysis, where variables "weak_lift" and "strong_lift" are the incremental signal contributed within the weak- and strong-genetic-prior strata. Variable "block" in that sheet partitions the perturbational block into its six constituent feature groups and does not refer to the three evidence blocks of the other sheets; the observational features are not included in it.

column2: Recovery at depth=panelD_recovery.csv;ROC curves=heldout_trial_roc_curves.csv;Discrimination statistics=heldout_trial_stats.csv;Score distribution=score_by_group.csv;Group summary=score_by_group_summary.csv;Group tests=score_by_group_tests.csv
column3: Recovery of held-out in-trial targets and score distribution by drug status
column4: Provided as external file. Ranking depths are described in the recovery sheet, one row per depth. Variable "k" is the nomination depth with variable "depth" its display label; variables "genetics" and "genetics_perturbseq" account for the number of the 727 held-out in-trial genes recovered by the genetics-only and full models respectively, and variable "gain" their difference. The discrimination sheet describes the held-out in-trial task by variables "model", "fpr" and "tpr", giving the false- and true-positive rates of each model's receiver operating characteristic curve; those curves are thinned to about 1,400 points each for plotting, so an area recomputed from them differs from the reported value in the fifth decimal place. The AUCs, their DeLong confidence intervals and the paired DeLong test are computed on the full curves and are reported in the accompanying statistics sheet by variables "statistic", "model", "value", "ci_lo" and "ci_hi". The score-distribution sheet describes all 19,502 genes: variable "grp" is the drug-status group, variables "pu_score" and "rank_pctile" the published model score and its rank percentile, and variables "pu_score_cv" and "rank_pctile_cv" the cross-fitted score and its rank percentile. The published score is the one the nominations rank on, and it scores the approved genes in sample, because they are training positives on every PU-bagging iteration. The cross-fitted score removes that: five folds are taken over the approved positives, each positive scored by the one fold that held it out and every other gene by all five, so that no group is scored by a model trained on it. Figure 4d plots "rank_pctile_cv", and every quantity in the group-summary and group-tests sheets is computed on the cross-fitted score rather than the published one. Group sizes, medians, means and quartiles are reported in the group-summary sheet, and the Kruskal-Wallis test across groups in the group-tests sheet, which also carries the one-way ANOVA, the one-sided Mann-Whitney test of held-out in-trial against non-target genes, and the three pairwise Mann-Whitney tests with Holm-Bonferroni-corrected p-values in variable "p_holm" and their annotation in variable "stars". Only the three pairwise tests are corrected, so "p_holm" is empty on the other rows. The two Mann-Whitney rows over the in-trial and non-target groups are complementary rather than duplicated: their U statistics sum to the product of the two group sizes and their p-values differ by a factor of two, because the held-out test is one-sided and takes in-trial as the first group. Figure 4d annotates the two-sided pairwise row, not the one-sided row; the one-sided test is retained here because the two U statistics check each other.

Provided as external file. Permutations are described in the null sheet, one row per permutation. Variable "perm" is the permutation index, and variables "genetic", "genetic+observational", "genetic+perturbational" and "full" give the AUC obtained by each model variant under that reassignment of positives. The summary sheet describes each tested quantity: variable "metric" names the model variant, variable "kind" records that the quantity is a level, variable "observed" is the observed value, variables "null_mean", "null_sd" and "null_p95" describe the null distribution, variable "emp_p" is the empirical p-value computed with the continuity-corrected estimator, and variable "n_perm" accounts for the number of permutations drawn (1,000). The four observed levels are identical to the corresponding cross-validated AUCs of the model ladder in Supplementary Table 6, and every empirical p-value re-derives exactly from the draws in the null sheet. No difference between two variants is tested in this sheet: label permutation drives every variant to chance, so such a comparison would ask whether an increment could arise when nothing predicts anything rather than whether functional genomics adds to genetics; the scrambled-feature control in the third sheet is that test. The scrambled-feature control is reported in the accompanying sheet, in which true labels and true genetic features are held fixed while the 19 functional-genomic features are row-permuted over 99 draws; variable "kind" separates the observed increment from the individual draws and the summary, variable "key" gives the draw index or the summary quantity, and variable "value" the increment in AUC. Its empirical p-value of 0.010 is the floor attainable with 99 draws; it is rank-based and no z-score should be computed from the dispersion of the draws.

column3: Genes ranked discordantly by the genetics-only and full models
column4: Provided as external file, one sheet per analysis. All 19,502 genes are described in the scatter sheet: variables "pctile_genetics" and "pctile_full" are the rank percentiles under the two models, variable "rank_shift" their difference, variable "core" the discordance label of the gene (promoted for the 36 genes rising across the boundaries, demoted for the 13 falling, none for the remaining 19,453), variable "gen_dec" the gene's genetic-prior decile, and variable "cov_class" its annotation-coverage class. The 49 promoted and demoted genes are those that invert across the 25th and 75th percentile boundaries. The core-gene sheet describes those 49 genes with their genetic and functional-genomic values ("IEI", "gwas_score", "mis.z_score", "lof.oe_ci.upper", "expected_n_regulators_residuals") and status flags ("is_druggable", "is_approved", "is_trial_heldout"). The feature sheet describes each tested feature by variables "direction" (promoted or demoted), "block", "n_sel", "med_sel" and "med_ctrl" (group size and median in the selected and matched-control sets), "rank_biserial" (effect size), "p" and "fdr", the last corrected within direction. The driver sheet reports variables "rho", "p" and "n_nonnull" for the correlation of each feature with rank shift. Network sheets describe the STRING protein-protein interaction test by variables "n_mapped", "n_edges", "null_mean_edges", "fold", "p_empirical" and "n_null_draws", with edge and node listings in variables "a", "b", "score" and "degree". The Gene Ontology sheet reports variables "direction" (promoted or demoted), "go_id", "term", "k_fg", "n_fg", "k_bg", "n_bg", "odds_ratio", "p", "fdr" and "n_family", where the "_fg" and "_bg" suffixes denote the foreground and background gene sets; the test is computed in both directions against a background of non-discordant genes measured in both functional-genomics blocks. Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied across every biological-process term whose annotated universe holds between 10 and 500 genes, a term-size filter fixed in advance and independent of the foreground count, giving the family size recorded in "n_family" (1,410 promoted, 1,409 demoted); rows are listed only where at least three foreground genes carry the term. One promoted term, defense response to virus, reaches an FDR below 0.05, and no demoted term does. Annotation-coverage sheets report variables "n_dark" and "pct_dark" for genes without a Gene Ontology biological-process term in each of five groups, with variables "OR_vs_promoted" and "fisher_p" comparing the promoted set against each of the four reference groups; those variables are empty on the promoted row itself, which is the reference. The stratified validation sheet reports variables "gen_stratum", "pct_up", "pct_down", "k_up", "k_down", "odds_ratio" and "fisher_p" per genetic-prior stratum. Protein-protein interaction evidence was derived from STRING and annotations from the Gene Ontology Consortium. The 49 marked genes are defined by the quadrant rule at the production seed alone; 10 lie within 0.01 of a boundary and the set is therefore not reseed-stable.

column3: Top 50 IGNITE nominations and bootstrap trial enrichment
column4: Provided as external file. The three sheets correspond one-to-one to the three panels of Figure 5 and are named for them. The first sheet, for panel a, describes the top 50 nominations excluding already approved immune targets, one row per nomination. Variable "rank_nonapproved" is the nomination rank after removal of approved targets, variable "pu_role" the gene's role in model fitting, and variable "furthest_imm_stage" the furthest immune-indication trial stage where present and empty otherwise. Variables "pu_score", "rank_pctile" and "rank" give the model score and its genome-wide rank and percentile, and variables "crossdonor_confidence" and "donor_vetted" the cross-donor reproducibility annotation of the perturbation signature; "donor_vetted" bins that correlation at 0.3 and records the 37 genes with no measured cross-donor correlation as not_measured rather than as weak, absent evidence and weak evidence being different claims. Nine of the 50 carry an immune-indicated drug in trial, all of which were held out from training. The second sheet, for panel b, describes the bootstrap enrichment of the top 50 nominations of each model at two trial-stage thresholds, one row per combination of variable "model" and variable "threshold" and one row per bar of that panel. Variable "model" is the full model or the genetics-only model of Supplementary Table 7, and variable "threshold" is Phase 1 or later for any immune trial, or Phase 3 or later for advanced immune trials. Each model is compared against 10,000 draws of 50 control genes sampled from its own non-approved genes ranked outside its own top 200, so that a fold is never reported against a null it was not computed from; the two control pools contain the same 18,962 genes in a different order and their base rates differ by less than 0.04 percentage points, which is why the figure draws a single control bar per threshold. Variables "observed_count" and "expected_count" give the observed and expected numbers of the 50 with such a drug, variables "observed_pct" and "expected_pct" the same quantities as percentages, variable "fold_enrichment" their ratio, and variables "ci95_lo_pct" and "ci95_hi_pct" the 2.5-97.5% bootstrap interval. The control quantities are a mean and percentiles over the rates of the 10,000 draws and are therefore reported as percentages, the expected count being that percentage applied to the 50 and so fractional. Variable "p_bootstrap" is the empirical proportion of draws reaching the observed rate, not the continuity-corrected estimator used in Supplementary Tables 7 and 8. Variable "p_bootstrap_bh" is that proportion after Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the eight enrichment tests displayed in Figure 5, and is the value the figure prints; correction is applied once across both panels because the top-50 comparison is shown in each of them. The remaining variables record the analysis settings: the sizes of the nomination set, of each control draw and of the bootstrap, the rank floor and size of the control pool, and the random seed. The third sheet, for panel c, repeats the any-immune-trial arm of the second across shortlist depth, one row per combination of variable "depth" (25, 50 or 100) and variable "model" and one row per bar of that panel. Its columns carry the same quantities as the sheet above, with three differences. Variable "threshold" is constant at Phase 1 or later, recorded so that the sheet states what it measures when read on its own; the advanced-trial threshold is absent because panel c does not plot it. Each control draw is the size of the shortlist it is compared against rather than a fixed 50, so that a shortlist of 100 is read against an interval of the same width, and the draw size is therefore given by variable "depth" and no fixed count is reported. The advanced-trial threshold is omitted rather than merely unplotted because its observed counts are 2 to 6 genes against an expectation of between 0.34 and 1.35, so its fold is unstable and the ordering between the two models is not consistent across the three depths; those quantities are computed at every depth and are available in the analysis outputs accompanying the code, and only the depth-50 values, which panel b draws, are reported here in the sheet above. The rows at depth 50 are the same computation as the corresponding rows of that sheet, not a second estimate, and are asserted equal to them when the sheets are built. The two shortlists are not independent samples: they share 27 of their 50 genes at depth 50, and 12 of 25 and 52 of 100 at the other two, so each row states whether that shortlist is enriched relative to chance and a difference between two rows is not a test of one model against the other.

column3: Comparison against published genetic priority scores with and without leakage control
column4: Provided as external file. Each score-by-evaluation combination is described in the comparison sheet, one row per combination. Variable "method" names the score: "PU full model" is IGNITE, "GPS overall" the maximum per-gene Genetic Priority Score (GPS), and "missense-z" is a single-feature comparator, the gnomAD missense Z-score. Variable "evaluation" is the test set, "standard_taskA" for all 727 held-out in-trial genes and "leakage_controlled" for the set of 535 in-trial genes unseen as positives by either method. Variable "auc" is the AUC, variables "n_genes" and "n_pos" the size of the evaluated universe and of the positive set, variable "missing_policy" the handling of genes without a score, and variable "note" any qualification applying to that row. The missing policy differs by method and is load-bearing: a gene with no published GPS score is scored as zero, because absence there means the score was never published rather than that the gene lacks the property, while a missing missense Z-score is dropped, which is why "n_genes" is not constant down the sheet. Paired DeLong statistics for the contrast of IGNITE against GPS are reported in the statistics sheet by variables "arm", "statistic" and "value", one block per evaluation arm: variable "arm" names the test set using the same labels as "evaluation" in the comparison sheet, and the statistics reported per arm are the two AUCs, their difference, z, the raw p, that p after Holm-Bonferroni correction across the two arms in "delong_p_holm", and variable "significance", the marker drawn on the figure, which is decided on the corrected value. The AUCs there are unrounded and round to the corresponding rows of the comparison sheet. The contrast is not significant on the standard arm (0.637 versus 0.641, raw p = 0.73) and is on the leakage-controlled arm (0.645 versus 0.592, raw p = 2.9 x 10-4; Holm-corrected 5.7 x 10-4), which is the comparison the analysis exists to make. Neither marker changes under the correction. Variable "arm" is empty on the single row reporting the number of model features, which is a property of the model rather than of an arm. Variable "gps_drug_labeled_gene" in the third sheet lists the 453 genes used as positive drug labels in GPS training. 192 of those 453 are held-out in-trial genes, and removing them is what takes the positive set from 727 to 535. A further 92 are unlabeled genes, so the evaluated universe falls from 19,162 to 18,878; of the rest, 161 are approved targets already excluded from both arms and 8 are absent from the 19,502-gene feature matrix. GPS values were derived from Duffy et al., 2024.

column3: Prospective temporal holdout composition and results
column4: Provided as external file. All 19,502 genes at the headline freeze year T0 = 2014 are described in the scoring sheet: variables "score_full", "rank_pctile_full", "score_genetics" and "rank_pctile_genetics" give the scores and rank percentiles of the full and genetics-only models retrained on pre-T0 labels, and variables "is_pos_at_T0", "is_emergent", "is_holdout" and "in_pool" indicate whether the gene was a training positive at T0, an emergent gene, an excluded labelled target, or a member of the unlabeled evaluation pool. The first, third and fourth of those partition the 19,502 genes as 259, 674 and 18,569, and the 134 emergent genes are a subset of the pool. The emergent-gene sheet describes those 134 genes, with variable "first_trial_year" the earliest trial start year across drugs annotated to that gene in any condition, not only the immune indication and the two rank percentiles repeated from the scoring sheet, ordered by full-model percentile. The headline sheet gives each model's emergent-versus-pool AUC at T0 = 2014 in variable "auc" with the permutation-null p-value in variable "p_emp" and the emergent count in "n_emergent". The sensitivity sheet describes freeze years 2013 to 2017, one row per year: variable "T0" is the freeze year, variable "n_P" accounts for the number of training positives, variable "n_emergent" for the number of emergent genes, variables "auc_full" and "auc_genetics" give each model's AUC, variable "delta" their difference with standard error in variable "se_delta", variables "delong_p_two_sided" and "delong_p_one_sided" the paired DeLong p-values, variables "ci95_lo" and "ci95_hi" the 95% CI of the AUC difference, and variable "p_full" the permutation-null p-value for the full model. The two permutation p-values are drawn at different depths and are both floors at zero exceedances: "p_emp" in the headline sheet is 1/10,001 over 10,000 permutations, "p_full" in the sensitivity sheet 1/5,001 over 5,000, so they differ by a factor of two without disagreeing. Trial dates were derived from the Open Targets Platform 26.06.

column3: Immune- and cardiac-exclusive recovery sets and performance
column4: Provided as external file. Each score-by-recovery-set combination is described in the performance sheet, one row per combination. Variable "recover" names the recovery set, "immune_exclusive" (n = 372) or "cardiac_exclusive" (n = 114), and variable "score" the prioritization score evaluated: "our_model" is IGNITE, and "OT_genetic_immune" and "OT_genetic_cardiac" are the Open Targets immune and cardiac genetic-association scores. Variable "auc" is the AUC with variables "ci_lo" and "ci_hi" bounding its 95% CI from 2,000 bootstrap draws and variable "ci" the same interval formatted for display, and variable "n_pos" the number of positives in that set. The comparison sheet describes each pairwise test: variable "panel" is the recovery set, variables "A" and "B" the compared scores with their AUCs in "auc_A" and "auc_B", variable "delta" the difference, and variables "z", "p", "p_holm" and "sig" the DeLong statistic, its raw p-value, that p-value after Holm-Bonferroni correction, and the significance annotation. Correction is applied within each recovery-set panel, over the three pairwise comparisons that panel makes, rather than across all six tests. A gene was considered immune-exclusive if an immune-indication drug against it had reached trial stage (Phase 1, 2 or 3) and it was neither in trial nor approved for a cardiac indication, and conversely for cardiac-exclusive genes. Genes with an approved drug in the area being recovered are excluded from the positive set rather than counted in it: the approved immune targets are the model's own training positives, so recovering them would not test specificity. Including them would give 447 and 176 positives instead of the 372 and 114 evaluated here. The shared negative pool comprises the 18,259 genes unlabeled in both indication areas. Indication annotations were derived from the Open Targets Platform 26.06.

Provided as external file, one sheet per evidence type. The evidence-axis sheet describes the percentile of STAT4 on each of four evidence axes: variable "axis" is the display label, variable "feature" the feature-matrix column the percentile is computed from, variable "percentile" that percentile taken among genes with a measured value for the feature, variable "evidence" the evidence block, and variable "order" the display order. Three of the four features are among the 24 modelled features of Supplementary Table 2; the Th17 axis uses "neglog10_adjp_Th17", the differential-expression significance, where the model itself uses the signed "zscore_Th17", because the axis reports how strongly knockdown shifts the Th17 program rather than in which direction. The disease sheet decomposes the model's immune-GWAS feature. It lists the 46 of STAT4's 1,164 Open Targets disease associations that carry fine-mapped GWAS credible-set evidence, by variables "disease" (Open Targets' own label, verbatim) and "label" (the form the figure draws: the same string shortened for four ontology ids, keyed on the id rather than the name so that a rename between releases cannot silently drop a row, and then capitalised at the first letter of each word, which leaves acronyms and hyphenated parts such as "ACPA+", "ALL" and "B-cell" as they are), "efo" the ontology id, "gwas_credible_sets_score" the credible-set datasource score and "overall_assoc_score" the overall association score, "tag" whether the disease falls inside the immune-system-disorder subtree MONDO:0005046 by its Open Targets ancestor list, "contributes_to_gwas_score" whether its evidence rolls into the model's feature, "n_credible_sets" how many credible sets it contributes, "best_l2g" the highest locus-to-gene score among them, and "credible_sets" the sets themselves, named by their Open Targets study-locus identifier and separated by "; ". They are ordered by locus-to-gene score descending with the identifier as tie-break, so the first set named is always one achieving the "best_l2g" reported beside it, and each identifier resolves at platform.opentargets.org/credible-set/. The study-locus identifier is used rather than the more readable study accession or lead variant because it is the only one of the three that is unique within a disease: the 32 sets under systemic lupus erythematosus arise from 27 distinct studies and 16 distinct lead variants, and all three sets under Graves disease share lead variant rs11889341, so a column built from either would name fewer sets than "n_credible_sets" counts. The variable is empty for the 25 diseases outside the immune subtree, which means they contribute no set to the feature and not that they carry none of their own. The 115 sets counted across the 21 contributing diseases are 110 distinct ones, four being shared between diseases because a set is counted under every ontology term its study trait maps to; de-duplicating the column therefore gives 110 rather than 115. The feature the model trains on is the credible-set score for STAT4 against MONDO:0005046, and the 21 diseases with "contributes_to_gwas_score" = 1 are exactly those whose evidence constitutes it, carrying 115 credible sets between them; the figure draws those 21 alone. The remaining 25 are associations outside that subtree and are supplied for audit: they are not part of the feature, and the highest of them, hypothyroidism at 0.801, outscores every contributing disease while contributing nothing. Because the feature is defined as the MONDO:0005046 rollup, the immune identity of the contributing diseases is definitional rather than a finding; the quantity of interest is the composition. The knockdown-neighborhood sheet describes the six nearest approved immune targets by cosine similarity of transcriptome-wide knockdown signature: variable "gene" is the neighbor, variable "cosine" the similarity, and variables "mechanism" and "pathway" its annotation, those two being hand curation rather than derived quantities. The two drug variables are by contrast derived, from the Open Targets 26.06 approved-drug evidence for that target. Variable "approved_drugs" names every approved drug for the target, separated by "; ", ordered with drugs carrying an immune indication first and alphabetically thereafter, so that the list leads with the immune-approved drug wherever the target has one; CD3E accordingly lists ten and CD3G nine. Variable "approved_drugs_label" is the truncated form the figure draws, giving the first of those names followed by the number withheld as "+ N more"; it is derived from the same ordering, so its named drug is always the first entry of "approved_drugs" and its count is always one fewer than that list is long. Only drugs that reached approval are counted or named; assets still in trials are excluded. A third variable, "lead_drug", carried a single hand-picked drug per gene and was retired on 2026-08-31, when "approved_drugs" began listing them all. Summary statistics of the neighborhood test are reported in the accompanying sheet by variables "statistic" and "value": the focal gene and condition, the anchor set of 112 approved targets with a signature, the comparison distribution of 7,044 unlabeled genes with a signature, and that distribution's 95th percentile and median. The score-distribution sheet gives variables "gene" and "pu_score" for all 19,502 genes, against which the STAT4 score of 0.963 at rank 13 is positioned; those scores are identical to the corresponding column of Supplementary Table 1 and are repeated here so that the dossier stands alone. The perturbational evidence axis was derived from the rest, 8 h and 48 h conditions of the CD4+ T-cell perturb-seq resource; the knockdown signatures behind the neighborhood sheets are from the 48 h stimulated condition alone, with symbols harmonized against the HGNC complete gene set. External annotations were derived from the GWAS Catalog and the Open Targets Platform 26.06 and were not used as model features.

column3: Nearest approved immune-target knockdown neighbor by condition
column4: Provided as external file, one sheet per stimulation condition. Genes carrying a significant on-target CD4+ T-cell knockdown and their nearest approved immune-drug target in knockdown-signature space are described in the table, one row per perturbed gene, ordered by descending similarity. Variable "gene" is the perturbed gene and variable "kNN_max_score" the cosine similarity of its transcriptome-wide knockdown signature to the most similar approved immune target; the maximum is taken over the anchor set rather than a mean or a centroid, so that a single mechanistic match is not diluted against unrelated positives. Variable "nearest_immune_target" names the anchor achieving it. A gene is never its own neighbor and never its own strongest signal: each perturbed gene's own column is set to zero before the signatures are length-normalized and the diagonal is excluded, so that the similarity between two genes cannot be inflated by each knockdown being the largest effect in its own row. The anchor set is the 340 approved immune targets of Supplementary Table 1 (variable "pu_role" = P), intersected in each condition with the genes that carry a knockdown signature, since only those can serve as a neighbor; that intersection is 105 genes at rest, 112 at 8 h and 112 at 48 h. Variable "is_approved_target" marks the rows belonging to it, which are scored against the remaining anchors rather than excluded. Variable "drug_name" names approved drugs targeting the nearest anchor gene separated by "; ". Variable "immune_indications" is the immune indications annotated to drugs targeting the nearest anchor gene at any development stage, likewise separated. Only drugs that reached approval are named, taken from the Open Targets rollup at "furthest_stage" = Approved; assets still in trials are excluded from that column but not from the indications beside it, and an indication listed here is one of the target's immune indications rather than a claim that the named drug is approved for it. Both list columns are capped by the Open Targets rollup at 15 drugs and 12 indications per gene: the drug cap truncates 1 to 2 anchors per sheet and the indication cap 46 to 71 per cent of rows, so a list at either length is a sample of the target's annotations rather than the complete set. Variable "n_downstream_z3" counts the measured genes whose expression shifts by more than three standard deviations on knockdown, computed on the same self-zeroed signature, and is supplied so that a high similarity carried by a near-silent knockdown is visible as such; its median is 35, 36 and 38 across the three conditions. Variable "culture_condition" repeats the sheet's condition so that the three can be concatenated without loss. Signatures are the "zscore" layer, the log2 fold change divided by its standard error, across 10,282 measured genes, restricted to knockdowns significant on target in at least 50 cells and de-duplicated to one row per perturbed gene, which is why the three sheets differ in length; symbols were harmonized against the HGNC complete gene set. These values are a post-hoc interpretive annotation and not a screening score: held-out discrimination between genes carrying an immune-indication trial and unlabeled genes is approximately chance from this similarity, at areas under the curve of 0.47 to 0.53 under every cross-condition pooling scheme tested. That is why the quantity interprets individual candidates rather than ranking the genome, and why it is not among the 24 modelled features of Supplementary Table 2. The conditions are reported separately rather than collapsed, and the 48 h stimulated sheet is computed independently of, and agrees with, the knockdown-neighborhood sheet of the STAT4 dossier in Supplementary Table 14. Derived from the genome-scale CD4+ T-cell perturb-seq resource of Zhu, Dann et al., 2025, and the Open Targets Platform 26.06.
